 -versus-
 State of Odisha and another .... Opposite Party(s)
 Mr. S. Patra, Asc
 Coram: Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra
 Order

This is an application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
2.

The petitioner is an accused in connection with Badagada P.S. Case No.143 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.43 of 2024 for the offences under Sections 450/376(1)/506 of I.P.C.
read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act pending in the Court of the learned Additional District Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Berhampur.
He is aggrieved by the order dated 30.04.2024 passed by the learned Court below, whereby his bail plea has been rejected.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
4.

The prosecution story in brief is that on 28.03.2024 at about 12.30 P.M., the informant/victim lodged a report alleging therein that on 08.03.2024 at about 1.00 P.M., while she was alone in her house, taking opportunity of her loneliness, his middle sister's brother-in-law came to her house and locked the door from inside, hugged her and committed sexual assault on her without her consent and threatened to put acid on her, if she will disclosed the matter before anyone.

Hence, the F.I.R.
5.
The statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has been recorded.
She in her statement inter alia stated that the petitioner is the brother-in-law of her middle sister.

On the date of incident,
he entered into the house and forcibly committed sexual act on her.
The petitioner is 26 years old boy.

sentences.text: 1 6. Regard being had to the nature of accusation made against the petitioner, I am not inclined to admit the petitioner on bail at this stage.
However, liberty is granted to the petitioner to renew his bail plea before the Court below after the victim in this case is examined.
The trial Court is directed to do well to see that the victim is examined by giving preference over all other witnesses.
7. With this observation, the BLAPL is disposed of.

(S.S. Mishra) Judge Swarna Location: High Court of Orissa Gaya Naik vs State Of Odisha And Another .... ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85552869/
